- Primary objective: Ask recipients to verify their passport and visa now.
- Passport requirement: Passport must have at least six months validity remaining.
- Visa requirement: Check visa rules for your nationality (link will be provided).
- Documents to bring: Extra passport photos and photocopies of passport if needed.
- Emergency/urgent contact: Consulate of X, +34 91 XXX XXXX (full contact details to be posted later).
- On-travel-day contingency: If you encounter an issue, meet the organizer in the hotel lobby at 07:30 for assistance with letters of support and emergency contacts.
- Follow-up actions promised: Poster will send the embassy link and a quick checklist; full consulate details will be posted.
style_agnostic:
"Important Travel Update

As we approach our trip, it's essential to verify your passport and visa requirements to avoid any last-minute issues.

**Passport Requirements:**
- Ensure your passport has at least 6 months' validity remaining.

**Visa Rules:**
- Check the visa requirements for your nationality: [link will be provided]

**Travel Documents:**
- Bring extra passport photos and photocopies of your passport, if needed.

**Emergency Contact:**
- In case of an emergency, please contact the Consulate of X at +34 91 XXX XXXX.

**On-Travel-Day Contingency:**
- If you encounter any issues, meet our organizer in the hotel lobby at 07:30 for assistance with letters of support and emergency contacts.

We'll send you the embassy link and a quick checklist shortly, and we'll post the full consulate details. Please return to this post and confirm your passport and visa are in order. Thank you for your cooperation and we look forward to traveling with you!"

persona.demographics: Urban — born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil; of mixed Portuguese and Afro-Brazilian heritage; currently based in Barcelona, Spain (frequent travel across Europe, South America, and Asia)
persona.profession: Founder & Tour Director, VolleyVoyage — sports travel agency that organises volleyball-focused international tours and cultural programs
persona.education: BA Tourism Management, Universidade de São Paulo; Postgraduate Certificate in Sports Event Management, Loughborough University; IATA/UFTAA travel agent accreditation; First Aid & Crowd Safety certification
persona.socioeconomic_status: Upper Middle Income; Small Business Owner / Entrepreneur
persona.brief_background: Rafael turned a childhood obsession with beach volleyball and backpacking into a niche travel business that pairs tournament attendance with curated cultural experiences. He is constantly on the move — scouting venues, negotiating with local clubs and hotels, and designing hands-on itineraries — and prides himself on delivering seamless logistics with authentic local flavor. He loves building relationships with clients and local guides, but sometimes overcommits to growing the business and struggles to delegate.
persona.interests_lifestyle: beach volleyball coaching and pickup games, attending FIVB/continental tournaments, scouting local grassroots matches, language learning (Portuguese, Spanish, English), street and travel photography, surf trips, samba and live music nights, experimenting with local cuisines, cycling for city scouting, yoga for recovery

general_writing_style.tone: Warm, energetic and service-oriented with a confident, can-do attitude; communicates like a trusted local guide who also understands logistics and risk. Generally informal and friendly—open to rapport-building and storytelling—while remaining professional and detail-focused when discussing bookings, schedules or safety. Tends toward reassuring language (emphasis on reliability and authenticity) and will acknowledge constraints or follow up if overcommitted.
general_writing_style.syntax: Prefers clear, active sentences with a mix of short directives for action and slightly longer descriptive lines for itineraries or logistics; often uses parallel structures for lists (e.g., "flight, transfer, check-in"). Avoids passive voice and dense subordinate clauses except when explaining complex scheduling; parenthetical asides appear frequently to add local tips or contingency notes. Uses present tense for plans and simple future for commitments, making calls-to-action direct and time-bound.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Draws on travel, events and volleyball vocab: words like "itinerary", "PAX", "transfer", "accreditation", "PNR", "ground handler", "FIVB", "set", "serve", "lineup" and "clinic" are common. Mixes industry jargon with local terms and Iberian/Latin American touchstones — "praia", "playa", "pousada", "hostel/hostal", "sambadrome" — and prefers metric measurements (km, m, kg) and European time formats. Photography and scouting terms ("golden hour", "frame", "scout the court") appear when describing venue assessments or promo materials.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Uses contractions and conversational markers freely ("I'm", "we'll", "can't"); often begins casual messages with local greetings or interjections like "Bom dia", "Vamos", or "Heads up". Frequently uses short pragmatic phrases to structure updates: "Quick note:", "FYI:", "Nice one", and closing warmth like "Abraço" or "Cheers"; will ask engagement questions such as "Sound good?" or "You in?". Recurrent verbs include "lock in", "scout", "book", "confirm" and habitually reassures with "I'll follow up" or "I'll sort it out."

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: A concise logistics update posted to a private group of booked participants about schedule tweaks or transport details.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Clear, direct and time-focused tone that prioritizes actionable information; use bullet-style short sentences and parallel structures (present tense for current plans, simple future for what will be done). Keep reassuring parenthetical notes and an explicit follow-up promise.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Start with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:" or "FYI:" and use short commands and confirmations. Example phrases: "Quick note: transfer now at 09:30", "Bring your ID (passport ok)", "I'll follow up with the PNR". Rely on terse sentence fragments for steps ("Meet at reception. Board at 09:15. Check-in by 10:00.") and finish with a confirmation question such as "Sound good?"

Write a social media post

- Reconnect with followers/contacts who played on the beach court.
- Prompt engagement by asking followers to share a favourite moment from the trip.
- Collect photos or short memories (one line or one photo) from followers to inspire new itineraries.
- Offer two response options: reply publicly in the thread or send a direct message (DM).
- Close with a friendly sign-off and expectation of seeing people on court soon.

- The poster's name/sign-off: "Abraço, Rafael" and "see you on court soon."
- Activity yesterday: scouting a tiny beach ("praia") court in Cascais.
- The scouting instantly evoked memories of "golden-hour sets together" and caused "saudade" (nostalgia).
- Question to audience: "How's life on the sand for you these days?"
- Request: share your favourite moment from the trip—one line, one photo, whatever comes to mind.
- Examples of items to share: a snap from that night market or the final match.
- Response channels: DM it to me or reply here.
- Statement that hearing these memories helps shape new itineraries.
- Closing prompt/confirmation: "Sound good?"

We're updating our website and social media with fresh stories from past VolleyVoyage trips and we'd love to feature your experience.

Looking forward to hearing back from you!

Abraço, Rafael"

task_details: Write a warm invitation to past clients for an alumni event in Barcelona: casual beach or indoor pick-up game (date, time, location) followed by a samba/caipirinha social at a nearby bar. Write a social media post

- Purpose: Invite alumni to an evening meet-up in Barcelona that combines a casual pick-up game and a social at a nearby bar.
- Host: Rafael.
- Audience: Alumni (players and those who want to join just for the social).
- Date & time: Saturday at 18:00.
- Meeting location: Barceloneta.
- First activity: informal/casual pick-up game at Barceloneta.
- Second activity: after the game, go to a nearby bar with samba music and caipirinhas.
- RSVP: ask people to reply to the post or send a direct message to RSVP.
- Capacity constraint: players are limited — ask prospective players to let the host know if they want to play.

style_agnostic:
"Calling all alumni!

It's time to get together and have some fun in the sun! I'm hosting an evening meet-up in Barcelona on Saturday at 18:00, and I'd love for you to join us.

We'll start with a casual pick-up game at Barceloneta, where we can get some exercise and catch up with each other. Don't worry if you're not a pro – this is all about having a good time and enjoying the beautiful views.

After the game, we'll head to a nearby bar with samba music and caipirinhas, where we can relax and socialize. Feel free to bring a photo or a short story from your travels to share with the group.

If you're interested in playing, please let me know ASAP so I can get an idea of numbers. And if you're coming from out of town, I'd be happy to help arrange a transfer or a budget-friendly place to stay nearby.

Just reply to this post or send me a direct message to RSVP. Can't wait to see you all there!

Cheers,
Rafael"

Write a social media post that:

- Announces planning for the next season and requests audience input.

  - Brazil’s northeast coast (praias and samba)
  - The Greek islands (sunset sets and seafood)
  - Japan’s beach circuits (technique clinics and culture)
- Instructs voters to pick one option and give a one-sentence reason for their choice.

- Encourages quick replies or dropping an emoji for mobile users.
- Ends with a casual sign-off: “Abraço, Rafael.”

task_instruction: Invite clients to refer friends in exchange for a referral discount code.
task_details: Write a friendly referral request offering a discount: past clients who refer a friend who books a tour get a fixed discount (e.g., €100) on their next VolleyVoyage trip. Provide instructions: refer by forwarding a unique code or have friend mention the referrer during booking; include validity window and mention it stacks with early-bird offers. Encourage sharing stories and close with warm encouragement to reach out with questions.
personalized: Hola! Small favour: if you loved the trip, could you tell a friend? I’m offering €100 off your next VolleyVoyage when someone you refer books with us and mentions your name (or uses your unique code). The code is valid for bookings confirmed within six months and it stacks with our early-bird deals. Just forward this message or have them mention you at booking—easy. Your word is the best marketing we’ve got, and I’ll make sure your next trip is even better. Obrigado and abraço, Rafael
prompt:
Write a social media post

- Primary objective: encourage past customers who enjoyed their trip to refer friends who might book a VolleyVoyage.
- Incentive: €100 off the referrer's next VolleyVoyage.
- Redemption condition: the referred person must book with the company and either mention the referrer's name or use the referrer's unique code.
- Code validity period: valid for bookings confirmed within six months.
- Stacking: the €100 referral discount stacks with existing early-bird deals.
- How to refer/redeem: forward the message to a friend or have the friend mention the referrer at booking.
- Target audience: people who recently took a VolleyVoyage and had a positive experience.
- Sender details included in original post: greeting "Hola!", closing "Obrigado and abraço," and signed as Rafael.

Obrigado, abraço, Rafael

- Ask responders to say what felt safe and what didn’t; request specific examples.
- Encourage reporting anything that felt off.

persona.profession: Founder & Tour Director, VolleyVoyage — sports travel agency that organises volleyball-focused international tours and cultural programs
persona.education: BA Tourism Management, Universidade de São Paulo; Postgraduate Certificate in Sports Event Management, Loughborough University; IATA/UFTAA travel agent accreditation; First Aid & Crowd Safety certification
persona.socioeconomic_status: Upper Middle Income; Small Business Owner / Entrepreneur
persona.brief_background: Rafael turned a childhood obsession with beach volleyball and backpacking into a niche travel business that pairs tournament attendance with curated cultural experiences. He is constantly on the move — scouting venues, negotiating with local clubs and hotels, and designing hands-on itineraries — and prides himself on delivering seamless logistics with authentic local flavor. He loves building relationships with clients and local guides, but sometimes overcommits to growing the business and struggles to delegate.
persona.interests_lifestyle: beach volleyball coaching and pickup games, attending FIVB/continental tournaments, scouting local grassroots matches, language learning (Portuguese, Spanish, English), street and travel photography, surf trips, samba and live music nights, experimenting with local cuisines, cycling for city scouting, yoga for recovery

general_writing_style.tone: Warm, energetic and service-oriented with a confident, can-do attitude; communicates like a trusted local guide who also understands logistics and risk. Generally informal and friendly—open to rapport-building and storytelling—while remaining professional and detail-focused when discussing bookings, schedules or safety. Tends toward reassuring language (emphasis on reliability and authenticity) and will acknowledge constraints or follow up if overcommitted.
general_writing_style.syntax: Prefers clear, active sentences with a mix of short directives for action and slightly longer descriptive lines for itineraries or logistics; often uses parallel structures for lists (e.g., "flight, transfer, check-in"). Avoids passive voice and dense subordinate clauses except when explaining complex scheduling; parenthetical asides appear frequently to add local tips or contingency notes. Uses present tense for plans and simple future for commitments, making calls-to-action direct and time-bound.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Draws on travel, events and volleyball vocab: words like "itinerary", "PAX", "transfer", "accreditation", "PNR", "ground handler", "FIVB", "set", "serve", "lineup" and "clinic" are common. Mixes industry jargon with local terms and Iberian/Latin American touchstones — "praia", "playa", "pousada", "hostel/hostal", "sambadrome" — and prefers metric measurements (km, m, kg) and European time formats. Photography and scouting terms ("golden hour", "frame", "scout the court") appear when describing venue assessments or promo materials.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Uses contractions and conversational markers freely ("I'm", "we'll", "can't"); often begins casual messages with local greetings or interjections like "Bom dia", "Vamos", or "Heads up". Frequently uses short pragmatic phrases to structure updates: "Quick note:", "FYI:", "Nice one", and closing warmth like "Abraço" or "Cheers"; will ask engagement questions such as "Sound good?" or "You in?". Recurrent verbs include "lock in", "scout", "book", "confirm" and habitually reassures with "I'll follow up" or "I'll sort it out."

task_instruction: Prepare a recruitment message for a seasonal driver/assistant for regional tours in Spain.
task_details: Location: Spain (based in Barcelona). Dates: seasonal contract May–September. Role: drive 9-seat vehicle, manage gear (nets, balls, posts), set up courts, assist coaches and players, help with light admin on the road. Qualifications: valid EU driving license, clean driving record, comfortable with manual transmission, physically fit, basic English/Spanish. Compensation: hourly plus accommodation on long trips. Application: driving license scan and short intro. Contact: DM or email.

Valid EU driving license and a clean driving record are required (manual transmission comfort appreciated). DM me or email — vamos? Cheers, Rafael

Write a social media post

- Job: seasonal driver/assistant
- Location: based in Barcelona, for regional tours
- Dates: May–September (seasonal)
- Vehicle: drive a 9-seat van
- Main duties: manage and load gear (nets, balls, posts), set up courts, assist coaches and players, perform light administrative tasks while on the road
- Requirements: valid EU driving license, clean driving record; comfort driving manual transmission appreciated; physically fit for lifting; flexible with early starts; basic English and basic Spanish
- Compensation & benefits: paid hourly; accommodation provided on longer trips
- Application instructions: send a scan/photo of your license and a short introduction
- Contact: DM or email to Rafael

- Clean driving record
- Comfort driving manual transmission a plus

- Basic English and Spanish skills

- Paid hourly rate

If you're passionate about sports and have a can-do attitude, send us your application! Please DM or email a scan/photo of your license and a short introduction to Rafael. We can't wait to hear from you! #seasonaljob #drivingjob #barcelona #sportsjobs"

persona.brief_background: Rafael turned a childhood obsession with beach volleyball and backpacking into a niche travel business that pairs tournament attendance with curated cultural experiences. He is constantly on the move — scouting venues, negotiating with local clubs and hotels, and designing hands-on itineraries — and prides himself on delivering seamless logistics with authentic local flavor. general_writing_style.tone: Warm, energetic and service-oriented with a confident, can-do attitude; communicates like a trusted local guide who also understands logistics and risk. Generally informal and friendly—open to rapport-building and storytelling—while remaining professional and detail-focused when discussing bookings, schedules or safety. Tends toward reassuring language (emphasis on reliability and authenticity) and will acknowledge constraints or follow up if overcommitted.
general_writing_style.syntax: Prefers clear, active sentences with a mix of short directives for action and slightly longer descriptive lines for itineraries or logistics; often uses parallel structures for lists (e.g., "flight, transfer, check-in"). Avoids passive voice and dense subordinate clauses except when explaining complex scheduling; parenthetical asides appear frequently to add local tips or contingency notes. Uses present tense for plans and simple future for commitments, making calls-to-action direct and time-bound.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Draws on travel, events and volleyball vocab: words like "itinerary", "PAX", "transfer", "accreditation", "PNR", "ground handler", "FIVB", "set", "serve", "lineup" and "clinic" are common. Mixes industry jargon with local terms and Iberian/Latin American touchstones — "praia", "playa", "pousada", "hostel/hostal", "sambadrome" — and prefers metric measurements (km, m, kg) and European time formats. Photography and scouting terms ("golden hour", "frame", "scout the court") appear when describing venue assessments or promo materials.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Uses contractions and conversational markers freely ("I'm", "we'll", "can't"); often begins casual messages with local greetings or interjections like "Bom dia", "Vamos", or "Heads up". Frequently uses short pragmatic phrases to structure updates: "Quick note:", "FYI:", "Nice one", and closing warmth like "Abraço" or "Cheers"; will ask engagement questions such as "Sound good?" or "You in?". Recurrent verbs include "lock in", "scout", "book", "confirm" and habitually reassures with "I'll follow up" or "I'll sort it out."

contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Casual, visual and evocative with short descriptive phrases that highlight sensory details and process insights; use photography vocabulary and an informal tone. Keep sentences punchy and intersperse parenthetical local tips or quick logistics notes.

task_instruction: Compose a caption about setting up a training clinic area with gear and warm-up zones.
task_details: Photo caption showing Rafael arranging a training clinic warm-up area: sand rakes, nets, water stations, coach area, schedule board. Use present-tense action verbs, photography vocabulary sparingly, include a parenthetical note about recovery/yoga timing, and end with 'You coming?'.

prompt:
Write a social media post

- Objective: inform followers that the clinic/session setup is complete and invite them to attend.
- Facts to include:
  - Sand has been smoothed with rakes.
  - Cones mark warm-up lanes.
  - Water station is live/available.
  - Clinic schedule is pinned on the coach board.
  - Coach microphone tested and is clear and loud.
  - Recovery mat area is set up.
  - Quick yoga slot scheduled at 09:30 (noted as helpful for tight shoulders).
  - Sessions are ready.
  - Call to action asking if the reader will attend.
style_agnostic:
"CLINIC SETUP IS COMPLETE! 

Get ready to take your game to the next level! Our clinic/session setup is now complete and we can't wait to see you there!

- The sand has been smoothed out with rakes, making it perfect for your drills and exercises.
- Cones mark out the warm-up lanes, so you can get moving and grooving in no time!
- Our water station is live and ready to quench your thirst.
- The clinic schedule is pinned up on the coach board, so you can plan out your day.
- The coach microphone has been tested and is clear and loud, so you won't miss a single tip or instruction.

- And, don't forget to join us for a quick yoga session at 09:30 - perfect for loosening up those tight shoulders!

Our sessions are ready to go, and we can't wait to see you there! Will you be attending? Let us know in the comments! #ClinicSetup #GetReady #TakeYourGameToTheNextLevel"

prompt:
Write a social media post

Key objectives and factual information:
- Celebrate a five‑year anniversary (“Cinco anos” / five years).
- Address or greet the community (original opens with “Bom dia”).
- Summarize accomplishments over the five years: courts scouted, pousadas found, strangers becoming teammates.
- Thank specific groups: people who travelled, coaches, volunteers, and those who shared a night of música.
- Announce an upcoming initiative: a new South America route.
- Describe the new route’s components: grassroots matches, surf mornings, and cultural nights.
- Include a closing/cheer (original ends with “Cheers”).
- Original text includes Portuguese words/phrases: “Bom dia,” “Obrigado,” and “música.”
style_agnostic:
"Bom dia, amigos! 

Can't believe it's already been Cinco anos since we started this incredible journey! We've come a long way, and we're so grateful for the amazing community that's grown alongside us. 

Over the past five years, we've scouted courts in every corner of the country, found the most incredible pousadas, and turned strangers into teammates. We couldn't have done it without the people who traveled with us, our incredible coaches, our selfless volunteers, and everyone who shared a night of música with us. Obrigado to each and every one of you!

But we're not slowing down yet! We're excited to announce our new South America route, packed with grassroots matches, surf mornings, and cultural nights that will take you on an unforgettable adventure. Stay tuned for more details and get ready to join the fun!

Cheers, and here's to many more years of making memories together!"

Tone: energetic and grateful. Include '1,000 PAX' phrasing, thank-yous, mention a photo gallery of highlights and a call-to-action to click the gallery link. Close with 'Abraço'. Use one emoji maximum.
personalized: 1,000 PAX — we hit the thousand mark! Obrigado a todos who trusted us to bring you to courts, local festas and golden-hour frames. I put together a photo gallery of favourites (scouts, sets, smiles) — link in bio. Next up: a mini-gallery just for behind-the-scenes scouting shots. Abraço
prompt:
Write a social media post

- Key objectives:
  - Announce and celebrate reaching the 1,000 PAX milestone (the thousand mark).
  - Thank the audience/clients for trusting the creator to bring them to shoots/locations.
  - Inform followers that a photo gallery of favourites has been put together and is available (link in bio).
  - Tease an upcoming mini-gallery dedicated to behind-the-scenes scouting shots.

- Factual information extracted from the original post:
  - Milestone: 1,000 PAX.
  - Thank-you phrasing used in Portuguese: "Obrigado a todos".
  - Locations/themes featured in the gallery: courts, local festas, golden-hour frames.
  - Types of images highlighted: scouts, sets, smiles.
  - Current gallery: a curated photo gallery of favourites (link in bio).
  - Next release: a mini-gallery of behind-the-scenes scouting shots.
  - Closing sign-off in Portuguese used in the original: "Abraço".
style_agnostic:
"Reaching the 1,000 PAX milestone is a dream come true and we couldn't have done it without YOU! Obrigado a todos for trusting us to bring you to these incredible courts, local festas, and golden-hour frames. 

To celebrate, we're excited to share our curated photo gallery of favourites, featuring some of our favourite scouts, sets, and smiles. Check it out (link in bio) and get ready to be transported to these amazing moments.

But that's not all - stay tuned for our upcoming mini-gallery dedicated to behind-the-scenes scouting shots, where you'll get a sneak peek into the making of these unforgettable moments.

Muito obrigado again for being part of this journey with us. Abraço!"

persona.name: Rafael Mendes
persona.demographics: Urban — born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil; of mixed Portuguese and Afro-Brazilian heritage; currently based in Barcelona, Spain (frequent travel across Europe, South America, and Asia)
persona.profession: Founder & Tour Director, VolleyVoyage — sports travel agency that organises volleyball-focused international tours and cultural programs
persona.education: BA Tourism Management, Universidade de São Paulo; Postgraduate Certificate in Sports Event Management, Loughborough University; IATA/UFTAA travel agent accreditation; First Aid & Crowd Safety certification
persona.socioeconomic_status: Upper Middle Income; Small Business Owner / Entrepreneur
persona.brief_background: Rafael turned a childhood obsession with beach volleyball and backpacking into a niche travel business that pairs tournament attendance with curated cultural experiences. He is constantly on the move — scouting venues, negotiating with local clubs and hotels, and designing hands-on itineraries — and prides himself on delivering seamless logistics with authentic local flavor. He loves building relationships with clients and local guides, but sometimes overcommits to growing the business and struggles to delegate.
persona.interests_lifestyle: beach volleyball coaching and pickup games, attending FIVB/continental tournaments, scouting local grassroots matches, language learning (Portuguese, Spanish, English), street and travel photography, surf trips, samba and live music nights, experimenting with local cuisines, cycling for city scouting, yoga for recovery

general_writing_style.tone: Warm, energetic and service-oriented with a confident, can-do attitude; communicates like a trusted local guide who also understands logistics and risk. Generally informal and friendly—open to rapport-building and storytelling—while remaining professional and detail-focused when discussing bookings, schedules or safety. Tends toward reassuring language (emphasis on reliability and authenticity) and will acknowledge constraints or follow up if overcommitted.
general_writing_style.syntax: Prefers clear, active sentences with a mix of short directives for action and slightly longer descriptive lines for itineraries or logistics; often uses parallel structures for lists (e.g., "flight, transfer, check-in"). Avoids passive voice and dense subordinate clauses except when explaining complex scheduling; parenthetical asides appear frequently to add local tips or contingency notes. Uses present tense for plans and simple future for commitments, making calls-to-action direct and time-bound.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Draws on travel, events and volleyball vocab: words like "itinerary", "PAX", "transfer", "accreditation", "PNR", "ground handler", "FIVB", "set", "serve", "lineup" and "clinic" are common. Mixes industry jargon with local terms and Iberian/Latin American touchstones — "praia", "playa", "pousada", "hostel/hostal", "sambadrome" — and prefers metric measurements (km, m, kg) and European time formats. Photography and scouting terms ("golden hour", "frame", "scout the court") appear when describing venue assessments or promo materials.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Uses contractions and conversational markers freely ("I'm", "we'll", "can't"); often begins casual messages with local greetings or interjections like "Bom dia", "Vamos", or "Heads up". Frequently uses short pragmatic phrases to structure updates: "Quick note:", "FYI:", "Nice one", and closing warmth like "Abraço" or "Cheers"; will ask engagement questions such as "Sound good?" or "You in?". Recurrent verbs include "lock in", "scout", "book", "confirm" and habitually reassures with "I'll follow up" or "I'll sort it out."

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: A celebratory milestone post announcing an anniversary, tour sold-out, or business achievement to the wider audience.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Upbeat, grateful and concise with a balance of excitement and humility; use short celebratory sentences, thank-yous, and a quick look-forward sentence about what's next. Keep the language inclusive and avoid boastful tones while using energetic punctuation and emojis selectively.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Start with a punchy opener and use collective pronouns and gratitude language. Example phrases: "We did it — sold out!", "Obrigado a todos", "Here's to more courts, more music, more stories". Use exclamation sparingly, close with "Abraço" or "Cheers", and include a mild forward-looking phrase like "Next up:"

task_instruction: Write a celebratory announcement for a newly launched destination that sold out immediately.
task_details: Audience: adventurous travellers and volleyball fans. Channel: Instagram caption and Twitter-friendly shortened version. Length: three short sentences. Tone: excited, humble, detail-focused. Include 'New destination — sold out!' phrase, mention scouting details (local clubs, courts, photography spots), thank local partners and participants, and include 'Next up:' with hint of expansion. Close with 'Abraço'. Emoji use optional.
personalized: New destination — sold out! Obrigado to the local clubs, hostal owners and everyone who jumped in; we scouted courts, mapped golden-hour photo spots and set up authentic cultural evenings. Next up: add a second departure and scout nearby towns for follow-ups. Abraço
prompt:
Write a social media post

- Announce that a new destination offering is sold out.
- Express thanks to local clubs, hostal/hostel owners, and everyone who helped/jumped in.
- State completed preparations: scouted courts, mapped golden-hour photo spots, set up authentic cultural evenings.
- Outline next steps: add a second departure and scout nearby towns for follow-up trips/events.
style_agnostic:
"UPDATE: Our highly anticipated destination offering has officially SOLD OUT!

We want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to the local clubs, hostal/hostel owners, and every single person who helped make this trip a reality. Your support and enthusiasm mean the world to us!

After weeks of preparation, we're thrilled to announce that all the hard work has paid off. Our team has scouted the most epic courts, mapped out the most stunning golden-hour photo spots, and set up authentic cultural evenings that will leave you with unforgettable memories.

Next steps? We're already planning to add a SECOND departure and are scouting nearby towns for our next follow-up trips and events! Stay tuned for more updates and get ready for the next adventure! #soldout #destinationoffering #newbeginnings"

Write a social media post

- List concrete benefits for our PAX: better room blocks, simplified accreditation, faster transfers.

We're thrilled to announce our new partnership with the top local club and the top local hotel!

"Beach Safety Reminder 

Heading to the playa this weekend? Don't forget these essential water safety tips:

 Swim only in flagged areas and follow lifeguard instructions - those red and yellow flags are there for a reason!

 Never swim alone - stay with a buddy!

 Don't swim after a night out or when you're sunburned - it's not worth the risk!

Safety First: Nights Out & Late Arrivals

As we head out for a night on the town, let's prioritize our safety above all else. 

When it comes to getting home, please only use our approved transport options: our buses, vetted taxis, or official ride-share apps. To ensure your ride is legit, always check the driver's plate and name against the booking.

Before you leave, remember to share your ETA with your group chat and send a quick ping when you arrive safely.

To stay safe on the streets:

- Avoid walking alone in unfamiliar or poorly lit areas.
- Travel in pairs or groups whenever possible.

When it comes to your belongings:

- Keep your passport and important documents locked in the hotel safe.
- Carry a photocopy or a digital photo of your ID.

In your room:

- Lock your door when you leave, and use the door chain if available.

If a ride feels unsafe, exit in a safe, public place and call our team at +34 600 123 456.

For immediate emergencies, call 112.

And don't worry, our team will be nearby and ready to help. If you need us, just ping us.

Let's look out for each other and have a safe and enjoyable night out!

As we prepare for our exciting adventure together, we want to emphasize the importance of prioritizing your health and medication management.

 Carry your prescription medications in their original packaging

Stay safe, stay healthy, and let's have an amazing time together!

Abraço
